answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because hollow only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, oasis is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any reef approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
